features: Cross-feature integration hardening: ensure Features 1.1–1.6 compose correctly under combined flag usage
End-to-end test coverage for multi-feature interactions (regression + refinement, sprint selection + lint-gate, diff + regression)
CLI help text and flag documentation for all Phase 1 Deepen flags
Edge case hardening: graceful behavior under adversarial or degenerate inputs across all new code paths

criteria.name: sprint_selection_with_regression_injection
criteria.description: When --sprint 3 is used and regression.json exists from sprints 1-2, the Evaluator prompt for sprint 3 includes accumulated behavioral regression criteria. An integration test in shared/ verifies this by simulating the harness flow: writing regression.json, then confirming buildRegressionSection output is non-empty and contains criteria from prior sprints.

criteria.name: sprint_selection_with_lint_gate
criteria.description: When --sprint N and --lint-gate are both set, the lint-gate hard mode still functions correctly: lint failure skips the Evaluator and counts as a failed attempt. No crash or undefined behavior from combining these flags. Verified by a test or code-path review showing lintGate logic is not bypassed by sprint-selection entry path.

criteria.name: refinement_preserves_regression_criteria
criteria.description: When --refine-spec triggers spec refinement after sprint N, the regression.json file is not modified or deleted. An integration test writes regression.json, calls freezeCompletedSprints and buildRefinementPrompt, then asserts regression.json contents are byte-identical before and after.

criteria.name: diff_and_static_analysis_coexist_in_evaluator_context
criteria.description: On retry attempt > 0, the Evaluator's supplementaryContext contains BOTH a '## Changes Since Last Attempt' diff section AND a '## Static Analysis Results' section (when both are available). The two sections do not clobber each other. Verified by reading harness.ts and confirming supplementaryContext is built by string concatenation of both sections.

criteria.name: regression_section_and_diff_section_ordering
criteria.description: The supplementaryContext string passed to the Evaluator has a consistent, deterministic ordering: regression criteria section appears before the diff section and before the static analysis section. This is verified by reading the harness.ts build-evaluate loop and confirming the append order.

criteria.name: all_new_cli_flags_in_help_and_documented
criteria.description: The flags --lint-gate, --sprint, --refine-spec, and --no-bdd are all (a) parsed in config.ts parseCli, (b) resolved in resolveConfig, (c) have corresponding fields on HarnessConfig in types.ts, and (d) appear with a human-readable description in the CLI help output (e.g., a helpText map, usage string, or --help handler). A grep or test confirms all four flags are present in all four locations.

criteria.name: combined_flags_no_crash
criteria.description: Passing --sprint 2 --lint-gate --refine-spec --no-bdd together does not cause a crash during config resolution. resolveConfig returns a valid HarnessConfig with sprint=2, lintGate=true, refineSpec=true, noBdd=true. A unit test in config.test.ts verifies this combination.

criteria.name: no_bdd_disables_regression_in_sprint_selection_mode
criteria.description: When --sprint 3 --no-bdd are combined, regression criteria are NOT injected into the Evaluator context even if regression.json exists. The guard `!config.noBdd && sprint > 1` in harness.ts covers this. Verified by code inspection or a test that simulates this path.

criteria.name: regression_json_survives_resume_and_sprint_selection
criteria.description: The regression.json file is not deleted by initWorkspace, cleanHarnessArtifacts, or any setup path triggered by --resume or --sprint. Verified by reading files.ts to confirm regression.json is excluded from cleanup, and by a test that writes regression.json then calls the cleanup function and asserts the file still exists.

criteria.name: invalid_sprint_values_handled_gracefully
criteria.description: Invalid --sprint values are handled gracefully without crashing: (a) --sprint 0 and --sprint -1 produce a clear error message or throw a descriptive error during config resolution, not an unhandled exception at runtime; (b) --sprint with a non-numeric value (e.g., --sprint abc) is rejected during CLI parsing or config resolution with a descriptive message; (c) a test or code-path review confirms these guards exist in parseCli or resolveConfig.

criteria.name: malformed_regression_json_handled_gracefully
criteria.description: If regression.json exists but contains invalid JSON or an unexpected schema (e.g., empty object, missing expected keys, truncated file), the harness does not crash with an unhandled exception. Instead it either (a) logs a warning and proceeds without regression criteria, or (b) throws a descriptive error that identifies the file as malformed. Verified by code review of the JSON.parse call site for regression.json showing a try-catch or schema validation, or by a test that writes malformed JSON and confirms graceful behavior.

criteria.name: existing_tests_still_pass
criteria.description: All existing tests in shared/*.test.ts pass when run with `bun test shared/`. No regressions introduced by sprint 5 changes. Exit code 0 from the test runner.

criteria.name: new_integration_tests_added
criteria.description: At least 3 new test cases (in existing or new test files under shared/) covering cross-feature interactions: (1) sprint selection + regression, (2) combined CLI flags, (3) refinement + regression preservation. Tests are runnable with `bun test` and pass.

criteria.name: type_safety_no_typescript_errors
criteria.description: Running `bunx tsc --noEmit` (or the project's typecheck script) produces zero type errors across shared/ and claude-harness/. All new code uses proper TypeScript types, no `any` casts introduced in sprint 5.

criteria.name: code_quality_no_dead_code_or_duplication
criteria.description: No unused imports, unreachable code, or duplicated logic blocks introduced in sprint 5. If refactoring consolidates existing duplication, it does so without changing behavior. Verified by code review of changed files.
